summary: The repeat of the corrected dual-majority experiment (receipt 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e) reproduced the same outcome under schedule variation, so the finding is not a single-run timing artifact: entry index 11, silent change committed on A and E, B elected in term 4 while A still led term 3, and the committed configuration entry truncated after healing. I then extended the probe to the client-facing consequence: a client command applied on the {A,B,E} leader after the silent change returns success and is committed with A and E, yet after the partition heals A's FSM still holds six applied commands while the new leader B holds five — the client's acknowledged write survives only on the node whose log lost the entry. The extended harness is submitted as a successor experiment with two comparisons (committed entry not truncated; FSMs equal after an acknowledged write); I dropped the 'at most one leader' comparison from it because a construction-time run showed A already stepping down before the old side's leader was sampled, and recorded that concurrency window as schedule-dependent rather than overstating it.
